question: Which exact P65 POSIX-open and cache retirement identities can the Resource Hook static test adapter use?

control_flow_evidence: POSIX 0x0c7357d4 body SHA256(first32)=ed11cc01bef28ef5c68f84cf46976e46af806905806b563fb6b96cdac1453412. Modes1/2/3 become native flags6/1/7, path is formatted with /%s, permissions0666, returns fd+1 or NULL.

Independent tests/firmware_p65.py executes exact firmware Thumb bodies with modeled OS/mutex/callback leaves. All8 tests pass including compiled adapter selective retirement and P65-shaped display/cache layouts.
Rejected old matcher candidates:0x1c1501d4 is socket code;0x00387db8 allocates LVGL object attributes. Neither may represent cache drop/release.
ownership_analysis: Firmware owns driver/caches and referenced decode payloads. Module replaces only its checked RAM callback slot, retires matching FILE keys, preserves references until native release, and refreshes serialized UI owners. No global cache purge or GPU fault guarantee.
unsafe_assumptions: Static recovery and modeled native-leaf tests do not establish a physical-device probe, production approval, or GPU recovery safety.
recommended_probe: Use an isolated P65 Mirage instance, then an explicitly authorized physical-device probe with the matching Supervisor; exercise repeated image changes, owner recreation, disable/re-enable and rollback.
